label: Allied Telesis AT-x530-10GHXm
description: Allied Telesis AT-x530-10GHXm compact stackable L3 switch: 8x 100M/1G/2.5G/5G PoE++ RJ-45 ports at up to 90 W each (720 W budget), 2x 1/10G SFP+ uplinks, 120 Gbps switching fabric, 89 Mpps.

poe.note: 720 W total, quoted by the vendor as 90 W x 8, from two fixed 500 W supplies. Every one of the 8 copper ports is a PoE++ (802.3bt) PSE port: 15.4 W PoE, 30 W PoE+, 60 W and 90 W PoE++ to 8 powered devices, PD classes 0-8, Mode A and Mode B wiring. The 720 W ceiling is the binding number, not the 1000 W of supply capacity: 8 x 90 W is all the PoE the chassis declares.

fabric.note: Vendor switching-fabric figure (forwarding rate 89 Mpps), the full-duplex aggregate of the port rates: 2 x (60000 Mbit/s of line rate).

notes: The compact half-width box: 441 x 421 x 44 mm, 6.6 kg, rack-mount ears included. The 8 x 100M/1G/2.5G/5G copper ports are ports 1-8 and the two SFP+ cages are ports 9 and 10 (9/S1 and 10/S2, the VCStack stacking ports by default). 2.5G/5G on copper is 802.3bz multi-gigabit, so a 2.5G link fits on Cat5e already in the wall. Two fixed non-replaceable PSUs; 73 W with no PoE load, 970 W fully loaded. Both SFP+ cages can be configured as 1G/10G Ethernet ports once VCStack is disabled. Console is the front-panel RJ-45 RS-232 port (AlliedWare Plus default 9600 8-N-1, no flow control; the switch ships with the manager/friend logins), reached with the RJ-45-to-DB-9 cable in the box or an AT-VT-Kit3 USB-to-serial cable. The management panel also carries a USB port and the eco-friendly button; neither is a network interface, so neither is modelled. Numbers: the x530 Series datasheet SPECIFICATIONS and Power and Noise tables and the model page at https://www.alliedtelesis.com/us/en/products/switches/x530-series; port numbering from the x530 Quick Installation Guide (https://www.alliedtelesis.com/sites/default/files/file/2022-03/ati-x530-english-qig.pdf) and, for the 10/18/28GSX/DP port fronts, the VCStack installation guide (https://www.alliedtelesis.com/sites/default/files/documents/installation-guides/ati_x530_vc_stacking_ig.pdf).

label: Allied Telesis AT-x530-18GHXm
description: Allied Telesis AT-x530-18GHXm stackable L3 switch: 16x 100M/1G/2.5G/5G PoE++ RJ-45 ports (1000 W budget; 60 W on all 16, 90 W on 11), 2x 1/10G SFP+ uplinks, 200 Gbps switching fabric, 149 Mpps.

poe.note: 1000 W total from two fixed 500 W supplies. Vendor budget table: 15.4 W PoE to 16 powered devices, 30 W PoE+ to 16, 60 W PoE++ to 16, but 90 W PoE++ to only 11 of the 16 - so the per-port figure modelled here is 60 W, the rate every port can hold at once. All 16 ports are 802.3bt PSE ports, PD classes 0-8, Mode A and Mode B.

fabric.note: Vendor switching-fabric figure (forwarding rate 149 Mpps), the full-duplex aggregate of the port rates: 2 x (100000 Mbit/s of line rate).

notes: 1U full-width: 441 x 421 x 44 mm, 6.7 kg. No front-panel figure for this model was found in the guides checked, so the 1-16 / 17-18 numbering follows the family pattern confirmed by the VCStack guide, which names 17/S1 and 18/S2 as the stacking ports. The 16 multi-gigabit copper ports are ports 1-16, the two SFP+ cages are ports 17 and 18 (17/S1 and 18/S2, stacking by default). 130 W with no PoE load, 1400 W fully loaded. The 90 W figure is a budget consequence, not a port limit: 11 x 90 W is 990 W and a twelfth port at 90 W would overrun the 1000 W ceiling. Console is the front-panel RJ-45 RS-232 port (AlliedWare Plus default 9600 8-N-1, no flow control; the switch ships with the manager/friend logins), reached with the RJ-45-to-DB-9 cable in the box or an AT-VT-Kit3 USB-to-serial cable. The management panel also carries a USB port and the eco-friendly button; neither is a network interface, so neither is modelled. Numbers: the x530 Series datasheet SPECIFICATIONS and Power and Noise tables and the model page at https://www.alliedtelesis.com/us/en/products/switches/x530-series; port numbering from the x530 Quick Installation Guide (https://www.alliedtelesis.com/sites/default/files/file/2022-03/ati-x530-english-qig.pdf) and, for the 10/18/28GSX/DP port fronts, the VCStack installation guide (https://www.alliedtelesis.com/sites/default/files/documents/installation-guides/ati_x530_vc_stacking_ig.pdf).

label: Allied Telesis AT-x530-52GPXm
description: Allied Telesis AT-x530-52GPXm stackable L3 PoE+ switch: 40x 10/100/1000T PoE+ RJ-45, 8x 100M/1G/2.5G/5G PoE+ RJ-45 (48 PoE+ ports, 740 W), 4x 1/10G SFP+ uplinks, 240 Gbps switching fabric, 179 Mpps.

poe.note: 740 W from two fixed 370 W supplies - not 48 x 30 W. The vendor budget table gives 48 ports at 15.4 W PoE but only 24 ports at 30 W PoE+, and the installation guide states the same ceiling as "up to 24 Class 4 powered devices at 25.5 W". Every one of the 48 copper ports is a 30 W-capable IEEE 802.3af/at PSE port, so the per-port figure modelled is 30 W and the 740 W budget is what stops a full 30 W fill at 24 ports: 48 x 30 W would need 1440 W.

fabric.note: Vendor switching-fabric figure (forwarding rate 179 Mpps), the full-duplex aggregate of the port rates: 2 x (120000 Mbit/s of line rate).

notes: All 48 copper ports are PSE ports (40 gigabit ports 1-40 plus 8 multi-gigabit ports 41-48); the four SFP+ cages 49-52 are not. 441 x 421 x 44 mm, 6.9 kg, 88 W with no PoE load, 970 W fully loaded, 42 dBA. The 5.4.8-2 stand-alone installation guide carried its multi-gigabit limitation note only for the 28-port chassis (ports 21-24); no equivalent note for ports 41-48 was found in the guides checked here, so the current datasheet figure of 100M/1/2.5/5G is what is modelled. Console is the front-panel RJ-45 RS-232 port (AlliedWare Plus default 9600 8-N-1, no flow control; the switch ships with the manager/friend logins), reached with the RJ-45-to-DB-9 cable in the box or an AT-VT-Kit3 USB-to-serial cable. label: Allied Telesis AT-x530DP-28GHXm
description: Allied Telesis AT-x530DP-28GHXm stackable L3 PoE++ switch with dual hot-swap PSU bays: 20x 10/100/1000T, 4x 100M/1G/2.5G/5G (24 PoE++ ports at up to 60 W), 4x 1/10G SFP+ uplinks, 1480 W PoE with two PWR1200 supplies, 160 Gbps, 119 Mpps.

poe.note: The budget is a function of the supplies fitted, not a fixed number: 370 W with one PWR800, 740 W with one PWR1200 or two PWR800s, 1480 W with two PWR1200s (datasheet PSU table). 1480 W is recorded here because it is the ceiling; the same chassis with a single supply has a quarter of the PoE. At 1480 W: 60 W PoE++ (802.3bt, PD classes 0-8) to all 24 ports, 30 W to all 24, 15.4 W to all 24.

fabric.note: Vendor switching-fabric figure (forwarding rate 119 Mpps), the full-duplex aggregate of the port rates: 2 x (80000 Mbit/s of line rate).

notes: The DP models replace the two fixed supplies with dual hot-swappable PSU bays (AT-PWR150 / PWR250 / PWR800 / PWR1200, standard or reverse-flow fans), which is the whole difference from the 28GPXm: same 24 copper ports and 4 SFP+ cages, but 20 x 1G plus 4 multi-gigabit and PoE++ rather than 24 x PoE+. Port numbering as the 28-port chassis: 1-20, 21-24, SFP+ 25-28 (27/S1, 28/S2 stacking by default; no DP front-panel figure was found in the guides checked here, so the numbering follows the 28-port chassis). 441 x 421 x 44 mm, 5.4 kg, 63 dBA with two PWR1200s. Vendor caution: hot-swapping a Class 5-8 PD can damage the PSE IC if the cable is pulled while power is applied, so disable the port first. Console is the front-panel RJ-45 RS-232 port (AlliedWare Plus default 9600 8-N-1, no flow control; the switch ships with the manager/friend logins), reached with the RJ-45-to-DB-9 cable in the box or an AT-VT-Kit3 USB-to-serial cable. The management panel also carries a USB port and the eco-friendly button; neither is a network interface, so neither is modelled. Numbers: the x530 Series datasheet SPECIFICATIONS and Power and Noise tables and the model page at https://www.alliedtelesis.com/us/en/products/switches/x530-series; port numbering from the x530 Quick Installation Guide (https://www.alliedtelesis.com/sites/default/files/file/2022-03/ati-x530-english-qig.pdf) and, for the 10/18/28GSX/DP port fronts, the VCStack installation guide (https://www.alliedtelesis.com/sites/default/files/documents/installation-guides/ati_x530_vc_stacking_ig.pdf).
